rule: Let A = the 'items' array of worker-enumeration.json in the trial workspace (the E-A enumeration) and B = the 'items' array of the child's enumeration.json (the E-B enumeration). Both are lists of strings; comparison is exact string equality. Compute setA = set(A), setB = set(B), U = sorted(setA union setB) ascending by code point. Overwrite result.json fields deterministically: result.items := U; result.single_source_items := sorted list of every string in exactly one of setA, setB (empty array when none), each annotated as {"item": <string>, "found_only_by": "worker"|"child"}; result.complete := true if setA == setB, otherwise false (a completeness claim is admissible only when both enumerations support it; a symmetric-difference item means at least one enumeration missed it or invented it, so completeness is not corroborated). result.method := existing method string + ' | E-B: ' + child enumeration.json method string + ' | E-C: deterministic set union per child/integration-plan.json'. No judgment is exercised at any step.

expected_contribution.Q2: The child's enumeration.json is the second, causally independent enumeration of the parse space: the child receives only package/artifacts/grammar.md and package/artifacts/expression.txt per child-input-manifest.json, never the worker's enumeration or intermediate work, so its item set settles whether an independent derivation yields the same set.
expected_contribution.Q3: The deterministic union rule above consumes the child's item set to produce the final merged items, the single-source flags, and the corroborated (or refuted) completeness boolean that this session left PENDING-INTEGRATION.
